question: In which year was Ujala Yojana launched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2015.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The UJALA (Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs for All) Yojana was launched by the Government of India on 1 May 2015, under the Ministry of Power. (उजाला योजना — 2015)

 

• It is implemented by Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL) and aims to promote the use of efficient LED bulbs in place of incandescent/CFL bulbs to reduce electricity consumption and carbon emissions.

 

• The scheme was earlier launched as the DELP (Domestic Efficient Lighting Programme) before being renamed and scaled up as UJALA.

 

• Under UJALA, India ran the world's largest LED bulb distribution programme, distributing LED bulbs at highly subsidised rates to domestic consumers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• EESL is a joint venture of NTPC, PFC, REC and POWERGRID, functioning under the Ministry of Power.

 

• UJALA is credited with substantial annual energy savings and reduction in peak electricity demand across India.

 

NOTE

 

• 2014 (Option 1): UJALA had not yet been launched in this year.

 

• 2016 (Option 2): Incorrect year; the scheme was already running by then.

 

• 2017 (Option 4): Incorrect year; UJALA was launched two years earlier.

question: Which of the following schemes of the Government of India is a part of the ‘Target Group’ approach?
option_4: Command Area Development & Water Management Programme (CADP)
solution_text:
The correct answer is Marginal Farmers Development Agency (MFDA).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rural development programmes in India are broadly classified into the Area Development Approach and the Target Group Approach. The Marginal Farmers Development Agency (MFDA), launched during the Fourth Five Year Plan to specifically assist marginal farmers, is an example of the Target Group Approach. (लक्ष्य समूह उपागम — सीमांत कृषक विकास अभिकरण)

 

• Under the Target Group Approach, programmes are designed for a specific category of beneficiaries (such as small/marginal farmers or agricultural labourers) regardless of where they live, rather than for a defined geographic area.

 

• MFDA (also referred to in some sources as the Marginal Farmers and Agricultural Labourers Agency, MFAL) provided credit and input support to identified marginal farmer households.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Small Farmers Development Agency (SFDA), launched alongside MFAL in 1970-71, is another example of the Target Group Approach.

 

• Programmes such as DPAP, HADP and CADP instead follow the Area Development Approach, which focuses on a defined backward or problem-prone geographic region.

 

NOTE

 

• DPAP (Option 1): The Drought Prone Areas Programme targets drought-affected areas, an area-based approach.

 

• HADP (Option 3): The Hill Areas Development Programme targets hilly regions, an area-based approach.

 

• CADP (Option 4): The Command Area Development Programme targets irrigation command areas, an area-based approach.

question: How many athletes were selected to represent India at the 1924 Paris Summer Olympics?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India sent a contingent of 8 athletes to the 1924 Paris Summer Olympics, competing in track and field (athletics) events. (1924 पेरिस ओलंपिक — 8 खिलाड़ी)

 

• This was one of India's earliest Olympic appearances, following its first participation in 1900 (Norman Pritchard) and the 1920 Antwerp Games.

 

• The Indian contingent did not win any medals at the 1924 Paris Games.

 

• India's Olympic participation became more organised in subsequent decades, with the Indian Olympic Association formally established in 1927.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's first Olympic medal came in field hockey at the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics, beginning a long era of Indian dominance in that sport.

 

• Norman Pritchard, who competed for India (then British India) at the 1900 Paris Olympics, remains India's first individual Olympic medallist (two silver medals in athletics).

 

NOTE

 

• 12 (Option 1): Not the correct figure for the 1924 Indian contingent.

 

• 10 (Option 2): Not the correct figure for the 1924 Indian contingent.

 

• 11 (Option 3): Not the correct figure for the 1924 Indian contingent.

question: For which of the following tribal music and dance forms was Arjun Singh Dhurve conferred with Tulsi Samman?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Baiga.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Arjun Singh Dhurve, a folk artist from Dindori district, Madhya Pradesh, is renowned for preserving and popularising the tribal Baiga music and dance tradition, for which he was conferred the Tulsi Samman by the Madhya Pradesh government. (तुलसी सम्मान — बैगा नृत्य)

 

• The Tulsi Samman is one of Madhya Pradesh's highest honours for contribution to the performing and plastic arts and literature.

 

• Arjun Singh Dhurve was also honoured with the Padma Shri in 2022 by the Government of India for his contribution to art (folk/tribal).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Baiga tribe, primarily found in Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, is known for its distinctive dance forms and body tattooing traditions.

 

• Other Madhya Pradesh state honours for art and culture include the Kalidas Samman and Tansen Samman.

 

NOTE

 

• Mardana (Option 1): Not the dance form associated with Arjun Singh Dhurve's Tulsi Samman.

 

• Pawara (Option 2): A folk dance form of tribal communities, but not the one for which Dhurve was honoured.

 

• Jhumta (Option 4): Not the dance form associated with Arjun Singh Dhurve's Tulsi Samman.

question: In November 2021, the government declared November 15 as ‘Janjatiya Gaurav Divas’. It happens to be the birth anniversary of which of the following freedom fighters?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Birsa Munda.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In November 2021, the Government of India declared 15 November as ‘Janjatiya Gaurav Divas’ (Tribal Pride Day), marking the birth anniversary of the tribal freedom fighter Birsa Munda. (जनजातीय गौरव दिवस — बिरसा मुंडा)

 

• Birsa Munda (born 15 November 1875) led the Munda Rebellion (Ulgulan) against British colonial rule and exploitative landlords in the Chotanagpur region.

 

• He is revered as ‘Bhagwan’ Birsa Munda among tribal communities of Jharkhand, Bihar, Odisha and West Bengal for his role in asserting tribal rights and identity.

 

• The day is observed to honour the rich cultural heritage and contribution of tribal communities to India's freedom struggle.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Birsa Munda's portrait is displayed in the Central Hall of the Indian Parliament in recognition of his contribution.

 

• Jharkhand's Birsa Munda Airport (Ranchi) and Birsa Munda Central Jail are named in his honour.

 

NOTE

 

• Kanhu Murmu (Option 2): A leader of the Santhal Rebellion (Hul, 1855), not the person whose birth anniversary is marked as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas.

 

• Arjun Munda (Option 3): A contemporary Indian politician (former Jharkhand CM and Union Minister), not the freedom fighter honoured on this day.

 

• Veer Narayan Singh (Option 4): A tribal freedom fighter of Chhattisgarh executed by the British in 1857, but not the person after whom Janjatiya Gaurav Divas is named.

question: Hola Mohalla is a festival associated with which religion/belief?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sikhism.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hola Mohalla is a Sikh festival, held annually a day after Holi at Anandpur Sahib, Punjab. (होला मोहल्ला — सिख धर्म)

 

• It was started by the tenth Sikh Guru, Guru Gobind Singh, in 1701, as a gathering of the Khalsa for displays of martial arts, mock battles, and physical strength.

 

• The festival features Gatka (traditional martial art) demonstrations, horse-riding, and other feats of valour, organised largely by the Nihang Sikhs.

 

• It reflects the martial and community spirit instilled by Guru Gobind Singh among the Khalsa Panth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Anandpur Sahib was founded by Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Sikh Guru, and is where the Khalsa Panth was created in 1699.

 

• Hola Mohalla concludes with a large procession (Nagar Kirtan) from the Takht Sri Keshgarh Sahib.

 

NOTE

 

• Jainism (Option 1): Its major festivals include Paryushana and Mahavir Jayanti, not Hola Mohalla.

 

• Islam (Option 2): Its major festivals include Eid and Muharram, not Hola Mohalla.

 

• Buddhism (Option 3): Its major festivals include Buddha Purnima, not Hola Mohalla.

question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts led to formation of the Goods and Services Tax Council?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 101st Constitutional Amendment Act.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016, introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India and provided for the constitution of the GST Council under Article 279A. (101वां संविधान संशोधन — जीएसटी परिषद)

 

• The GST Council, chaired by the Union Finance Minister, includes state finance ministers and makes recommendations on GST rates, exemptions, and related matters.

 

• GST was rolled out across India from 1 July 2017, subsuming multiple indirect taxes like VAT, excise duty and service tax.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 102nd Amendment Act (2018) gave constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC).

 

• The 103rd Amendment Act (2019) introduced 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS).

 

NOTE

 

• 102nd Amendment (Option 1): Relates to the NCBC, not GST.

 

• 100th Amendment (Option 2): Relates to the exchange of enclaves with Bangladesh (Land Boundary Agreement), not GST.

 

• 103rd Amendment (Option 4): Relates to EWS reservation, not GST.

question: Which acid is used as a souring agent added to vinegar, pickled vegetables, and sauces, and as a raw material for seasoning?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Acetic acid.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Acetic acid (CH₃COOH) is the acid responsible for the sour taste and pungent smell of vinegar, and is widely used as a souring/preservative agent in pickled vegetables, sauces, and food seasoning. (एसिटिक अम्ल — सिरका)

 

• Vinegar typically contains 4-8% acetic acid by volume, produced by the fermentation of ethanol by acetic acid bacteria.

 

• Besides food use, acetic acid is an important industrial chemical used in the manufacture of vinyl acetate, cellulose acetate, and various esters.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Citric acid occurs naturally in citrus fruits like lemon and orange and gives them their sour taste.

 

• Tartaric acid is found in grapes and is used in baking powder; formic acid is secreted by ants and some insects, causing a stinging sensation.

 

NOTE

 

• Citric acid (Option 1): The souring agent in citrus fruits, not the primary acid in vinegar.

 

• Tartaric acid (Option 3): Found in grapes/wine and used in baking, not the primary acid in vinegar.

 

• Formic acid (Option 4): Found in ant/insect stings, not the primary acid in vinegar.

question: Which coal is low-grade, brown and soft with high moisture content?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lignite.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lignite, also called brown coal, is a low-grade coal that is soft, brownish in colour, and has a high moisture content and low carbon content. (लिग्नाइट — भूरा कोयला)

 

• Lignite has a lower calorific value compared to bituminous coal or anthracite, and is mainly used for electricity generation near the mining site.

 

• Major lignite reserves in India are found in Tamil Nadu (Neyveli), Rajasthan, and Gujarat.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Coal formation follows an increasing order of carbon content and quality: Peat → Lignite → Bituminous → Anthracite.

 

• Anthracite is the highest-grade coal with the highest carbon content and calorific value, but is scarce in India (found mainly in Jammu & Kashmir).

 

NOTE

 

• Metallurgical (Option 1): Refers to coking coal (mainly bituminous grade) used in the steel industry, not a low-grade brown coal.

 

• Bituminous (Option 3): A medium-to-high grade coal, harder and more carbon-rich than lignite, most abundantly found and used coal in India.

 

• Anthracite (Option 4): The highest-grade, hardest coal with the least moisture, the opposite of lignite's characteristics.

question: Which of the following gases plays an important role in welding titanium, aluminium, stainless steel, and magnesium?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Argon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Argon, a chemically inert noble gas, is widely used as a shielding gas in welding processes such as TIG (Tungsten Inert Gas) and MIG (Metal Inert Gas) welding of titanium, aluminium, stainless steel, and magnesium. (आर्गन गैस — वेल्डिंग)

 

• Being inert, argon prevents the molten metal from reacting with atmospheric oxygen and nitrogen, avoiding oxidation, porosity and weakening of the weld.

 

• Argon is obtained industrially through the fractional distillation of liquid air, making up about 0.93% of the Earth's atmosphere.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Argon is also used in incandescent and fluorescent lighting to provide an inert atmosphere that protects the filament.

 

• Other noble gases — helium, neon, krypton, xenon, radon — are also chemically inert but are less commonly used for welding due to cost or reactivity considerations.

 

NOTE

 

• Fluorine (Option 1): A highly reactive halogen, unsuitable as an inert shielding gas.

 

• Neon (Option 2): An inert noble gas but mainly used in signage/lighting, not commonly for welding these metals.

 

• Chlorine (Option 4): A reactive halogen gas, unsuitable for welding shielding.

question: Which award was started by the Government of Madhya Pradesh in 1980 to the exponents of Hindustani classical music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tansen Samman.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Tansen Samman was instituted by the Government of Madhya Pradesh in 1980 to honour exponents of Hindustani classical music. (तानसेन सम्मान — हिंदुस्तानी शास्त्रीय संगीत)

 

• It is named after the legendary musician Mian Tansen, one of the ‘Navratnas’ of Emperor Akbar's court, who was born near Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh.

 

• The award is presented annually during the Tansen Sangeet Samaroh, a classical music festival held at Behat, Gwalior (Tansen's samadhi/tomb site).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Madhya Pradesh government honours for the arts include the Kalidas Samman (performing/visual arts and literature) and Lata Mangeshkar Samman (music).

 

• The Tansen Samman has also been extended over the years to honour Hindustani classical musicians from outside India as an international award category.

 

NOTE

 

• Kumar Gandharva Samman (Option 1): Not the award started in 1980 by the MP government for Hindustani classical music generally.

 

• Kishore Kumar Samman (Option 3): An MP state award related to playback singing/film music, not the 1980 Hindustani classical music award.

 

• Iqbal Samman (Option 4): An MP state award for Urdu literature, not for Hindustani classical music.

question: Where was the first successful textile mill established in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mumbai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first successful cotton textile mill in India, the Bombay Spinning and Weaving Company, was established in Mumbai (Bombay) in 1854 by Cowasjee Nanabhoy Davar. (प्रथम सफल वस्त्र मिल — मुंबई)

 

• Mumbai's favourable location — a port city close to cotton-growing regions of Maharashtra and Gujarat, along with capital from Parsi and Gujarati merchants — made it the hub of India's early cotton textile industry.

 

• Mumbai came to be known as the ‘Cottonopolis of India’ because of the rapid growth of the cotton textile industry there in the 19th century.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first jute mill in India was established near Kolkata at Rishra in 1855, marking the start of India's jute industry in Bengal.

 

• Ahmedabad later emerged as another major cotton textile centre, earning the title ‘Manchester of India’.

 

NOTE

 

• Kolkata (Option 1): Became the centre of India's jute industry, not the first successful cotton textile mill.

 

• Surat (Option 2): An important trading port historically, but not the site of India's first successful textile mill.

 

• Jaipur (Option 4): Not associated with the first successful textile mill in India.

question: Which of the following Acts gave the government enormous powers to repress political activities, and allowed detention of political prisoners without trial for two years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rowlatt Act, 1919.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rowlatt Act, 1919 (formally the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act) gave the colonial government sweeping powers to curb political activities and allowed detention of political prisoners without trial for up to two years. (रॉलेट एक्ट, 1919 — बिना मुकदमा नजरबंदी)

 

• It was based on the recommendations of the Rowlatt Committee, chaired by Justice Sidney Rowlatt, set up to examine revolutionary conspiracies.

 

• The Act triggered widespread protests across India, famously giving rise to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (13 April 1919) in Amritsar during protests against it.

 

• Mahatma Gandhi launched the Rowlatt Satyagraha, his first major all-India movement, in opposition to this Act.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rowlatt Act is often referred to by critics as the ‘Black Act’ or the ‘No-Vakil, No-Appeal, No-Daleel Act’ due to its harsh, arbitrary provisions.

 

• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre led to widespread condemnation, including Rabindranath Tagore renouncing his knighthood in protest.

 

NOTE

 

• India Contract Act, 1872 (Option 1): A civil law governing contracts, unrelated to political detention.

 

• Criminal Tribes Act, 1871 (Option 3): Branded certain communities as ‘born criminals’, but is distinct from the political-detention powers of the Rowlatt Act.

 

• Indian Slavery Act, 1843 (Option 4): Abolished certain forms of slavery in British India, unrelated to political detention.

question: The term Blue Line is associated with which of the following games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ice Hockey.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Ice Hockey, the Blue Lines are two lines drawn across the rink that divide it into three zones — the defending zone, neutral zone, and attacking zone — and are central to the sport's offside rule. (ब्लू लाइन — आइस हॉकी)

 

• A team is offside if an attacking player crosses the opponent's blue line before the puck does.

 

• The Red (Centre) Line and Goal Lines are other important markings on an ice hockey rink, alongside the two blue lines.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ice hockey is played between two teams of six players each (including a goaltender), using a rubber disc called a puck.

 

• Terms unique to ice hockey include ‘icing’, ‘power play’, and ‘hat-trick’ (originally popularised in this sport before spreading to others).

 

NOTE

 

• Football (Option 1): Uses terms like offside line/touchline, but not a ‘Blue Line’.

 

• Cricket (Option 2): Uses terms like crease and boundary, not a ‘Blue Line’.

 

• Table Tennis (Option 3): Played on a marked table with a net, no ‘Blue Line’ terminology.

question: According to the inscriptions, Pushyamitra Shunga was a devotee of which of the following Gods?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shiva.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pushyamitra Shunga, founder of the Shunga dynasty, overthrew the last Mauryan ruler Brihadratha around 185 BCE and is described in inscriptions and tradition as a devotee of Lord Shiva. (पुष्यमित्र शुंग — शिव भक्त)

 

• His reign marked a Brahmanical revival, with a renewed emphasis on Vedic rituals such as the Ashvamedha (horse sacrifice), which he is recorded to have performed, as attested by the Ayodhya inscription of Dhanadeva.

 

• This resurgence of orthodox Brahmanical Hinduism under the Shungas came after the strong Buddhist patronage of the preceding Mauryan emperor Ashoka.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ayodhya inscription of Dhanadeva records that Pushyamitra performed two Ashvamedha sacrifices, an important source for Shunga-era history.

 

• Later Shunga rulers, such as Bhagabhadra, are associated with Vaishnavism/Bhagavatism, as evidenced by the Heliodorus (Besnagar) Pillar.

 

NOTE

 

• Rama (Option 1): Not the deity associated with Pushyamitra Shunga in the inscriptions.

 

• Krishna (Option 3): Vaishnava/Bhagavata worship is instead associated with the later Shunga ruler Bhagabhadra (via the Heliodorus Pillar), not Pushyamitra.

 

• Indra (Option 4): Not the deity associated with Pushyamitra Shunga in the inscriptions.

question: What action was taken by the government to celebrate the achievement of the Green Revolution in agriculture?
option_1: Released a regular salary for the farmers
option_2: Distributed free food to all the people
option_4: Distributed green vegetables to the people
solution_text:
The correct answer is Released a special stamp, ‘Wheat Revolution’.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In July 1968, then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi released a special postage stamp titled ‘Wheat Revolution’ to officially mark India's impressive strides towards self-sufficiency in wheat production under the Green Revolution. (हरित क्रांति — गेहूं क्रांति डाक टिकट)

 

• The Green Revolution in India, associated principally with agricultural scientist M. S. Swaminathan and high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, transformed India from a food-deficit to a food-surplus nation, especially in wheat and rice.

 

• The revolution was concentrated initially in states like Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• M. S. Swaminathan is regarded as the ‘Father of the Green Revolution in India’, while Norman Borlaug is called the global ‘Father of the Green Revolution’.

 

• The Green Revolution began in India in the mid-1960s, with 1967-68 often cited as a landmark year for record wheat production.

 

NOTE

 

• Regular salary for farmers (Option 1): Not an action taken to mark the Green Revolution's achievements.

 

• Free food distribution (Option 2): Not the government's specific commemorative action for the Green Revolution.

 

• Distributed green vegetables (Option 4): Not the government's specific commemorative action for the Green Revolution.

question: Khudai Khidmatgars, a non-violent movement among the Pathans was started by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Khudai Khidmatgars (‘Servants of God’), a non-violent movement among the Pathans (Pashtuns) of the North-West Frontier Province, was founded by Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan in 1929. (खुदाई खिदमतगार — खान अब्दुल गफ्फार खान)

 

• Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan is popularly known as ‘Frontier Gandhi’ and ‘Badshah Khan’, owing to his close association with Mahatma Gandhi and commitment to non-violence.

 

• Members of the movement were also known as ‘Red Shirts’ (Surkh Posh) because of the colour of their uniform.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan was honoured with India's highest civilian award, the Bharat Ratna, in 1987 — the first non-Indian citizen to receive it.

 

• The Khudai Khidmatgars later allied closely with the Indian National Congress during the freedom struggle.

 

NOTE

 

• Alluri Sitarama Raju (Option 1): Led the Rampa Rebellion in Andhra region, unrelated to the Khudai Khidmatgars.

 

• Bakht Khan (Option 2): A key military leader of the Revolt of 1857 in Delhi, not the founder of the Khudai Khidmatgars.

 

• Sachindra Bakshi (Option 4): Associated with revolutionary activities (Kakori conspiracy era), not the founder of the Khudai Khidmatgars.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘The State shall, in particular, direct its policy towards securing that the ownership and control of the material resources of the community are so distributed as best to subserve the common good’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 39(b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 39(b) of the Indian Constitution, part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), directs the State to ensure that ‘the ownership and control of the material resources of the community are so distributed as best to subserve the common good’. (अनुच्छेद 39(ख) — भौतिक संसाधनों का समान वितरण)

 

• Article 39 lays down certain principles of policy to be followed by the State, aimed at securing social and economic justice.

 

• Article 39(b) and 39(c) together have been invoked in landmark Supreme Court cases relating to the distribution of resources and prevention of concentration of wealth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 39(a) directs the State to secure that citizens have an adequate means of livelihood.

 

• Article 39(c) directs the State to prevent concentration of wealth and means of production to the common detriment; Article 39(d) mandates equal pay for equal work for men and women.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 39(a) (Option 1): Deals with adequate means of livelihood, not distribution of material resources.

 

• Article 39(c) (Option 3): Deals with preventing concentration of wealth, a related but distinct clause.

 

• Article 39(d) (Option 4): Deals with equal pay for equal work, not distribution of material resources.

question: In the southern ranges of which hills is Mawsynram, which receives the highest rainfall in the world, located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khasi hills.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mawsynram, widely cited as the place receiving the highest average annual rainfall in the world, is located in the southern ranges of the Khasi Hills in the East Khasi Hills district of Meghalaya. (मासिनराम — खासी पहाड़ियाँ)

 

• Mawsynram's exceptional rainfall results from moisture-laden monsoon winds from the Bay of Bengal being forced upward by the funnel-shaped terrain of the Khasi Hills, causing intense orographic rainfall.

 

• Nearby Cherrapunji (Sohra), also in the Khasi Hills, is another location famous for extremely high rainfall and once held the ‘highest rainfall’ record itself.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Khasi, Jaintia, and Garo Hills together form the hill ranges of Meghalaya, a state whose name means ‘Abode of Clouds’.

 

• Meghalaya is one of the wettest regions in the world due to its unique topography and monsoon exposure.

 

NOTE

 

• Shevaroy hills (Option 1): Located in Tamil Nadu, unrelated to Mawsynram.

 

• Mizo hills (Option 2): Located in Mizoram, unrelated to Mawsynram.

 

• Naga hills (Option 4): Located along the Nagaland-Myanmar border, unrelated to Mawsynram.

question: India finished on which of the following positions in overall medals tally at Commonwealth games 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India finished 4th in the overall medal tally at the 2022 Commonwealth Games held in Birmingham, England, winning a total of 61 medals — 22 gold, 16 silver, and 23 bronze. (राष्ट्रमंडल खेल 2022 — भारत चौथे स्थान पर)

 

• Australia topped the medal table, followed by England in 2nd place and Canada in 3rd place, with India in 4th.

 

• India's strongest performances came in weightlifting, wrestling, badminton, table tennis, and boxing.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Star performers for India at CWG 2022 included Mirabai Chanu (weightlifting gold), P. V. Sindhu (badminton gold), and the Indian men's Table Tennis team (gold).

 

• The 2022 Commonwealth Games were the first CWG to feature more women's medal events than men's.

 

NOTE

 

• 3rd (Option 1): Incorrect; that position was held by Canada.

 

• 1st (Option 3): Incorrect; Australia topped the medal tally.

 

• 2nd (Option 4): Incorrect; that position was held by England.

question: To gain control over Kannauj the Tripartite Struggle was fought between which of the following dynasties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pratihara, Rashtrakuta and Pala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Tripartite Struggle, fought for control over the strategically and economically important city of Kannauj, involved three major powers: the Gurjara-Pratiharas, the Rashtrakutas, and the Palas. (त्रिपक्षीय संघर्ष — कन्नौज)

 

• This power struggle spanned roughly the 8th to 10th centuries CE, reflecting Kannauj's importance as a symbol of political supremacy in northern India.

 

• The Gurjara-Pratiharas ultimately held Kannauj as their capital for the longest period among the three rival dynasties.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rashtrakutas were based in the Deccan (with their capital at Manyakheta), while the Palas ruled over Bengal and Bihar with their capital at Pataliputra/Monghyr.

 

• The Pratihara ruler Mihira Bhoja is particularly noted for consolidating Pratihara control over Kannauj.

 

NOTE

 

• Solanki, Parmar and Chandella (Option 2): Regional dynasties of central/western India, not the parties to the Tripartite Struggle.

 

• Khalji, Tughlaq and Lodhi (Option 3): Delhi Sultanate dynasties from a later medieval period, unrelated to the Tripartite Struggle.

 

• Pallava, Pandya and Chola (Option 4): South Indian dynasties, not involved in the struggle for Kannauj.

question: Which of the following researchers observed densely stained reticular structures surrounding the nucleus (Hint: Figure)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Camillo Golgi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Italian scientist Camillo Golgi first observed densely stained, reticular (net-like) structures surrounding the nucleus of nerve cells in 1898, using a silver-staining technique he had developed; this structure was later named the Golgi apparatus (Golgi body/Golgi complex) in his honour. (गॉल्जी उपकरण — कैमिलो गॉल्जी)

 

• The Golgi apparatus is a cell organelle involved in modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for secretion or delivery to other organelles.

 

• Camillo Golgi was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1906 (shared with Santiago Ramón y Cajal) for his work on the structure of the nervous system.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Golgi staining technique (‘black reaction’), using silver nitrate, was pivotal in enabling detailed study of neuron structure.

 

• The Golgi apparatus is often described as the ‘packaging and dispatch centre’ of the cell.

 

NOTE

 

• William Harvey (Option 1): Known for describing the circulation of blood, not the Golgi apparatus.

 

• Francis Crick (Option 2): Co-discoverer of the structure of DNA (double helix), not the Golgi apparatus.

 

• Louis Pasteur (Option 4): Known for germ theory of disease and pasteurisation, not the Golgi apparatus.

question: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding circular flow of income?
option_1: Savings as well as government expenditure are injections to the circular flow.
option_2: The income of one sector becomes the expenditure of the other.
option_3: In a circular flow, leakages are equal to injections.
option_4: The real flow and monetary flow move in a circular manner in an opposite direction.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Savings as well as government expenditure are injections to the circular flow.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the circular flow of income, savings are a leakage (withdrawal) from the flow, not an injection, since money saved is taken out of the income-expenditure stream; government expenditure, on the other hand, is correctly classified as an injection. Because the statement wrongly clubs savings together with government expenditure as injections, it is NOT correct. (चक्रीय प्रवाह — बचत रिसाव है, इंजेक्शन नहीं)

 

• Leakages (withdrawals) from the circular flow include savings, taxes, and imports; injections into the flow include investment, government expenditure, and exports.

 

• In equilibrium, total leakages equal total injections, keeping the level of national income stable.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The circular flow of income has two components: the real flow (flow of goods and services/factor services) and the monetary flow (flow of money as payment), which move in opposite directions.

 

• The circular flow model is fundamental to understanding national income accounting in both two-sector and multi-sector (household, firm, government, foreign) economies.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2: Correctly describes the circular flow — one sector's income is another sector's expenditure — so this statement is correct, not the answer.

 

• Option 3: Correctly states that leakages equal injections in equilibrium, so this statement is correct, not the answer.

 

• Option 4: Correctly describes the opposite-direction movement of real and monetary flows, so this statement is correct, not the answer.

question: The type of reaction that is typically found when a material that is required for the reaction to proceed, such as a surface or a catalyst, is saturated by the reactants is called a __________ order reaction.
solution_text:
The correct answer is zero.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A zero order reaction occurs when the rate of reaction is independent of the concentration of the reactant(s), typically because a required surface or catalyst has become saturated by the reactants. (शून्य कोटि अभिक्रिया — उत्प्रेरक संतृप्त)

 

• In such cases, since the catalytic surface can only accommodate a fixed number of reactant molecules at a time, adding more reactant does not increase the reaction rate.

 

• The rate law for a zero order reaction is expressed as Rate = k[A]⁰ = k, meaning the rate equals the rate constant k and stays constant over time.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Examples of zero order reactions include certain enzyme-catalysed reactions at high substrate concentration and the photochemical reaction between hydrogen and chlorine.

 

• In a first order reaction, the rate is directly proportional to the concentration of one reactant; in a second order reaction, it depends on the concentration of two reactants (or the square of one).

 

NOTE

 

• First (Option 1): Rate depends on the concentration of a reactant raised to the first power, not applicable to a saturated-catalyst scenario.

 

• Second (Option 2): Rate depends on the concentration of reactant(s) raised to the second power (combined), not applicable here.

 

• Third (Option 4): A rare, high-order dependence on concentration, not applicable to a saturated-catalyst scenario.

question: The registered office of the Sangeet Natak Akademi is at:
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Delhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy for music, dance, and drama, has its registered office at Rabindra Bhavan, New Delhi. (संगीत नाटक अकादमी — नई दिल्ली)

 

• It was established by the Government of India in 1952, making it the first national academy of arts set up in independent India.

 

• The Akademi confers the prestigious Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Puraskar) and Akademi Fellowship (Ratna Sadasya) to recognise excellence in the performing arts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other national akademis headquartered in Rabindra Bhavan, New Delhi include the Sahitya Akademi (literature) and Lalit Kala Akademi (visual arts).

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi also confers the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar to encourage young talent in the performing arts.

 

NOTE

 

• Kolkata (Option 1): Not the location of the Sangeet Natak Akademi's registered office.

 

• Chennai (Option 3): Not the location of the Sangeet Natak Akademi's registered office.

 

• Mumbai (Option 4): Not the location of the Sangeet Natak Akademi's registered office.
